title: Intake from Conflicting Notes
scenario: It is 6:15 AM. Two overnight notes arrived and they do not agree. On top of that, neither note says how generation performed. Real intake is not extraction - it is deciding what is trustworthy, and being honest about what is missing.
input:
[5:40 AM] Overnight Desk Analyst:
ERCOT spiked overnight. Peak around $192/MWh, settled near $145. Trader flagged the spike for review - need approval before we act.

[6:05 AM] Overnight Desk Analyst:
Correction after final settlement: ERCOT peak confirmed at $192/MWh, settled at $141/MWh. No word yet on generation performance.

Desk rule: when notes conflict, the LATER note is authoritative. When a required fact is missing from every source, record null - never guess.
instructions: Compare the two notes field by field and apply the desk rule.
Where the later note corrects the earlier one, use the correction.
Generation performance appears in neither note - record null, not a guess.
Record which note time you treated as authoritative.
Return one JSON object, then validate.
copilotPrompt: Two notes conflict; the later one is authoritative. Extract hub, peakPrice, settledPrice, generationFlag, approvalRequired, and authoritativeNoteTime. Generation performance is stated nowhere, so generationFlag must be null - do not guess a value.
successMessage: Intake record built from conflicting sources - with the gap recorded honestly instead of papered over.

intro.heading: Before you build: trust is decided, not extracted

sections.title: Conflicting sources are normal
sections.body: At Easy tier the note was single and clean. Real mornings produce corrections, retractions, and follow-ups. The intake step's real job is deciding which value wins - and the desk rule (later note is authoritative) is a governed decision, not your judgment call.

sections.title: Null is a value, guessing is a bug
sections.body: Neither note says how generation performed. Writing null tells every downstream step 'this was checked and is unknown'. Writing a guess tells them a lie they cannot detect. Explicit nulls are how pipelines stay honest.

sections.title: Record your provenance decision
sections.body: authoritativeNoteTime captures WHICH source you trusted. When someone asks next week why the brief said 141 and not 145, the record answers without archaeology.

fieldGuide.meaning: The market hub both notes discuss.
fieldGuide.hint: Both notes agree on this one.

fieldGuide.meaning: The peak price from the authoritative source.
fieldGuide.hint: Check whether the correction changed it.

fieldGuide.meaning: The settled price from the authoritative source.
fieldGuide.hint: This is the field the notes disagree on.

fieldGuide.meaning: Generation performance - if any source states it.
fieldGuide.hint: Stated nowhere. What does the desk rule say to record?
The flag from the first note was never retracted.

fieldGuide.meaning: Which note you treated as the source of truth.
fieldGuide.hint: The desk rule decides this, not preference.

takeaway.heading: Intake built from conflict
points: You resolved a source conflict using a governed rule (later wins), not intuition.
You recorded an explicit null instead of a guess - downstream steps now KNOW generation status is unknown, rather than believing a fabrication.
You captured provenance (authoritativeNoteTime), so the record can defend itself under questioning.
The flag survived the correction: an unretracted escalation stays true.
The workflow can now build a trustworthy record even when its sources disagree.
